explanation: The response only recognizes the broad topic of toughness after thermal exposure and mentions an intervention-versus-control comparison. It does not provide a defined intervention, temperature window, mechanistic mediator, quantitative or directional prediction, evidence, or a discriminating falsification criterion. A valid reconstruction would specify intermediate-temperature aging, connect maximal L12 ordering and jagged FCC/B2 boundaries near 600 degrees C to planar slip, pile-ups, and embrittlement, and predict ductility recovery near 750 degrees C as ordering weakens and ductile transition zones form. A decisive test would combine mechanical testing across the aging window with TKD or TEM evidence of pile-ups and crack initiation at jagged phase-boundary tips while excluding impurity-segregation-driven intergranular fracture.
